people.name: Braxton Brackin
people.alt: Braxton Brackin in a pink western shirt and straw hat, holding a buckskin horse at a rodeo arena
people.bio: Raised around rodeo and riding for 27 years, Braxton learned calf roping from her uncle before she could walk. She still competes, and teaches with a firm but encouraging style that helps students believe they can do anything they set their minds to.

people.name: Anna Foote
people.alt: Anna Foote cheek to cheek with a dark horse with a white blaze, mountains behind
people.bio: Born and raised in Cody, Wyoming, Anna rode six years with a rodeo drill team before moving to Oklahoma after college in 2023. She loves breakaway roping and teaching riders of every age, and making it fun.

people.name: Chloe Bjornberg
people.alt: Chloe Bjornberg in a navy show jacket, standing with a dapple grey horse
people.bio: A former president of the OU Equestrian Team, Chloe has taught English and western lessons for over eight years. She's now in graduate school at OU, working toward becoming a counselor who offers equine-assisted therapy.

how._comment: The 'How it works' switch (header). Each note names the Station product behind a feature and says what it does ON THE LIVE SITE. Nothing on this preview is connected, so no note may claim a feature works now, or anything the products do not do. No invented prices or numbers. Features carry data-how=<key> in build.py; 'spots' are matched by selector for parts other scripts build. Rendered by _src/how.js.
how.legend: Each outlined part of this page is run by a Station product, named in the note beside it. This site is a preview, so nothing is connected yet: the notes say what happens on the live site.

herd: Every horse gets its own page, following it from the day it arrived to the day it is well.
The same story goes out as the ranch’s two-a-week horse series on Instagram and Facebook, scheduled from one calendar.
journal: Each step of the horse’s recovery, and what it cost, is added to this page as it happens.
The same updates go out as the two-a-week horse series on Instagram and Facebook, scheduled from one calendar.
The monthly email tells donors which horses moved forward and what their gifts paid for.
news: Each post here also goes out on Instagram and Facebook, scheduled from one calendar.
Once a month the news goes to everyone on the ranch’s email list.
join: The address joins the ranch’s own email list. Once a month, everyone on it hears how the horses are doing.
giver: Secure checkout on the ranch’s own Stripe account: card, Apple Pay, Google Pay or bank. The money goes straight to the ranch, and a tax receipt arrives by email at once.
Monthly donors change or stop their gift from the link in their receipt. A card that fails is retried automatically.
promise: Every donor gets a thank-you from Braxton within the hour. A gift of $250 or more also alerts Braxton to call the donor personally.
Donors get the horse updates, a summary of their giving each January, and the Giving Tuesday appeal.
A donor who has not given for 12 months gets a short note from the ranch inviting them back.
levels: A sponsorship is a monthly gift through secure checkout on the ranch’s own Stripe account, with a tax receipt by email. Sponsors change or stop it from their receipt link, and a failed card is retried automatically.
Each new sponsor gets a thank-you from Braxton within the hour.
The monthly note on the horse, the January giving summary and Giving Tuesday all go out by email.
logos: Radar finds local businesses that fit, like feed and tack stores, vet clinics and riding programs, and lines them up in the ranch’s sponsor pipeline for the ask.
A business sponsor can be sent an invoice and pay it online.
volunteer: Every sign-up gets a welcome by text and email the same day, and follow-ups until the volunteer replies.
The welcome links to the ranch’s booking page, where a new volunteer picks a first barn day and gets a reminder before it.
flyer: Families pick a lesson, camp or pony party and book it themselves, and reminders by text and email make sure they turn up.
where: The ranch’s Google listing is kept to one name, one address and one set of hours, with the donate and volunteer links and a horse update each week.
After a visit or a volunteer day, everyone who came is asked for a Google review, not only the happy ones. Braxton approves a drafted reply to each review.
call: When nobody can get to the phone, a missed call gets a text back within seconds.
An AI receptionist answers the ranch’s number, takes a message on surrender and welfare calls, and passes urgent ones straight to Braxton.
facts: Built by Station on the ranch’s own photos and words, and the ranch’s to keep.
The same name, address and phone are kept on the ranch’s Google listing, so the two never disagree.
links: Every social bio points here instead of Linktree, so a follower is one tap from Donate.
“Get the monthly update” turns a follower into someone on the ranch’s own email list.
greet: An AI assistant answers from the ranch’s own facts at any hour, and takes the visitor’s details so the ranch can follow up.
footer: The sign-up on the magenta sheet below joins the same monthly email list.
The ranch’s number gets missed-call text-back and the AI receptionist.
“donate.” goes to the same secure checkout on the ranch’s own Stripe account.
